symbols.name: Amax
symbols.role: upper bound for the reduced loading norm

symbols.name: WKDClass
symbols.def: \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{WKD}}\) is the class of laws generated by recursive additive-error structural equations \(Z_v=f_v(Z_{\operatorname{pa}(v)})+\epsilon_v\) with mutually independent centered coordinate errors, with order identifiability supplied by nonlinear structural functions or by linear non-Gaussian errors, as in Wang--Kolar--Drton

symbols.name: GammaOf
symbols.def: \(\Gamma(P)\) is the unique greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance attached to \(P\in\mathcal M\)

symbols.name: Dpi
symbols.def: \(D_\pi\) is the innovation-scale factor in the modified Cholesky decomposition in order \(\pi\)

symbols.name: Lpi
symbols.def: \(L_\pi\) is the unit-lower-triangular factor in the modified Cholesky decomposition \(\Gamma=L_\pi D_\pi^2L_\pi^\top\) in order \(\pi\)

symbols.name: W
symbols.role: one addable element on an ideal edge

symbols.name: Ideals
symbols.def: \(\mathcal J=\{J\subseteq A:J\text{ is an ideal of }\preceq|_A\}\)

symbols.name: KN
symbols.def: \(K_N=\{H\in\mathbb S_{++}^p:\lambda I\preceq H\preceq\Lambda I,\ \|H-\widehat\Gamma_N\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\Delta_N\}\) on the active branch

symbols.name: CN
symbols.type: measurable random compact subset of \(\mathbb R\)

symbols.name: bpath
symbols.role: singleton causal effect along the least-favorable path

symbols.name: spliceHandle
symbols.def: Smooth low-frequency Gaussian compensation of a Laplace--Student characteristic function, with a flat cutoff at frequency proportional to \(\sqrt{\log N}\), followed by a common Gaussian convolution kernel

symbols.name: HLap
symbols.def: \(H_{\mathrm{Lap}}\) has the centered standardized Laplace law

symbols.name: amin
symbols.role: lower bound for the treatment loading

symbols.name: d4
symbols.role: number of raw moments of total degree one through four

symbols.name: CLap
symbols.role: global propagation modulus across the cumulant floor and spectral-clipping kinks

symbols.name: hatGammaLap
symbols.def: Recover \(a_T=(\kappa_{TTTT}/3)^{1/4}\), \(a_i=\kappa_{iTTT}/(3a_T^3)\), and set \(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}=\operatorname{clip}_{[\lambda,\Lambda]}(\widehat{\operatorname{Cov}}(X)-\widehat a\widehat a^\top)\), using clipped empirical moments and a positive cumulant floor

symbols.name: CNlap
symbols.type: measurable random compact subset of \(\mathbb R\)

symbols.name: KReal
symbols.def: \(\mathcal K(\mathbb R)\) is the space of nonempty compact subsets of \(\mathbb R\) with its Hausdorff Borel sigma-field
symbols.role: codomain for fiber estimators and confidence sets

symbols.name: EstTheta

symbols.name: P1N
symbols.def: \((P_{1,N})_{N\ge1}\subset\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}\) is a law sequence to be derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:smooth\text{-}splice}\)

assumptions.condition: \(\preceq\) is a known strict partial order on \(V\).
\(\Gamma\) is the greatest covariance in Loewner order among Gaussian convolution divisors of \(P_X\).

novel.justification: This explicit model condition aligns the causal innovation covariance with the maximal Gaussian convolution component of the observed law. It holds for the stated Laplace-factor examples and for residual laws whose directional log characteristic-function modulus is subquadratic in every direction; it is not inferred from the finite-ray envelopes or attributed to the source-identification theorem.

assumptions.condition: The coordinates of \(H\) are mutually independent.
The first nonzero entry of each column of \(A\) is positive.
The columns of \(A\) are sorted in ascending lexicographic order.

novel.justification: After the unit-variance source normalization fixes scale, this bound is invariant to observationally irrelevant source signs and permutations and allows dense confounding while excluding genuinely diverging reduced-form loadings.

assumptions.condition: No coordinate of \(H\) has a nondegenerate Gaussian convolution divisor.

novel.justification: Three variables are the smallest dimension supporting a treatment, an outcome, and a nontrivial order-swap collision.

assumptions.condition: \(\preceq\) is the strict partial order whose only ordered pair is \(T\prec Y\).

novel.justification: A known temporal relation from treatment to outcome with one unordered intermediate variable is the minimal partial-order setting in which effect collisions arise.
The explicit covariance path remains uniformly above this fixed positive spectral floor.
The explicit covariance path remains uniformly below this fixed finite ceiling.
The smooth Laplace--Student family has a common polynomial characteristic-function lower envelope at this fixed value.
The smooth Laplace--Student family has a common polynomial characteristic-function upper envelope below this fixed value.
Exponent two is realized by Laplace tails on every named ray because all loadings on those rays are nonzero.
This fixed value contains the exact eighth moments of the proposed smooth splice and its Gaussian convolution.
The standardized rank-one loading path has norm strictly below this fixed value.
A literal standardized-Laplace factor is an auditable heavy-tailed parametric specification with a nonzero fourth cumulant.
A source that loads nontrivially on treatment is empirically meaningful for treatment confounding, and a fixed lower bound prevents the cumulant inversion from becoming singular.

definitions.name: Fourier-separated mixed-noise class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M(p,\lambda,\Lambda,c,C,Q,M_8,q,A_{\max},\preceq)=\{P_X:X=U+G_\Gamma,\ U=AH,\ U\perp G_\Gamma,\ \lambda I\preceq\Gamma\preceq\Lambda I,\ \Gamma\text{ is the greatest Gaussian divisor of }P_X,\ 1\le k\le p,\ H_1,\ldots,H_k\text{ are mutually independent, nonconstant, Gaussian-indecomposable, and unit variance},\ \operatorname{rank}(A)=k,\text{ the first nonzero entry of each column of }A\text{ is positive, the columns are in ascending lexicographic order},\ \|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le A_{\max},\ c(1+|t|)^{-q_u}\le|\phi_U(tu)|\le C(1+|t|)^{-q_u}\text{ for every }u\in\mathcal R\text{ and }|t|\ge1,\ \mathbb E\|X\|^8\le M_8,\ \preceq\text{ is a known strict partial order}\}\)

definitions.name: Exponent-two collision subclass
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_\star=\{P_X\in\mathcal M(3,1/10,4,2/5,60,2,50000000,q,3,\preceq):\preceq\text{ has only }T\prec Y,\ q_u=2\text{ for every }u\in\mathcal R\}\)

definitions.name: Centered Fourier covariance region
definitions.construction: If \(t_N\ge1\) and \(m_N\ge2\varepsilon_N\), set \(z_u=-2t_N^{-2}\{\log(\max(|\widehat\phi_N(t_Nu)|,m_N/2))+q_u\log(1+t_N)-(\log c+\log C)/2\}\), \(w_N=t_N^{-2}\{\log(C/c)+4\varepsilon_N/m_N\}\), polarize by \((Z_N)_{ii}=z_{e_i}\) and \((Z_N)_{ij}=(z_{e_i+e_j}-z_{e_i}-z_{e_j})/2\), set \(\Delta_N=3pw_N/2\), set \(\widehat\Gamma_N=\operatorname{clip}_{[\lambda,\Lambda]}(Z_N)\), and set \(K_N=\{H:\lambda I\preceq H\preceq\Lambda I,\ \|H-\widehat\Gamma_N\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\Delta_N\}\). Otherwise set \(\widehat\Gamma_N=((\lambda+\Lambda)/2)I\) and \(K_N=\{H:\lambda I\preceq H\preceq\Lambda I\}\).

definitions.name: Whole-fiber confidence region
definitions.construction: On the active branch set \(C_N=\bigcup_{J\in\mathcal J}[\beta_J(\widehat\Gamma_N)-2L_\beta\Delta_N,\beta_J(\widehat\Gamma_N)+2L_\beta\Delta_N]\cap[-\Lambda/\lambda,\Lambda/\lambda]\). On the fallback branch set \(C_N=[-\Lambda/\lambda,\Lambda/\lambda]\).

definitions.name: Smooth-splice lower-experiment handle
definitions.construction: Smooth low-frequency Gaussian compensation of a Laplace--Student characteristic function with six Student degrees in the polynomial tail, a cutoff proportional to \(\sqrt{\log N}\), and a common Gaussian convolution kernel along \(\Gamma(s)=\Gamma_\star+saa^\top\).

definitions.name: Measurable fiber-estimator domain
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak E_{\Theta,N}=\{\widetilde\Theta_N:(\mathbb R^p)^N\to\mathcal K(\mathbb R):\widetilde\Theta_N\text{ is Borel measurable}\}\).

definitions.name: Uniform whole-fiber honesty
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(\mathcal M_\star)=\{(S_N)_{N\ge1}:S_N:(\mathbb R^p)^N\to\mathcal K(\mathbb R)\text{ is Borel measurable and }\liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}P^{\otimes N}\{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\subseteq S_N\}\ge1-\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: Exact-collision law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}=\{P\in\mathcal M_\star:\exists s\in[0,1]\text{ such that }\Gamma(P)=\Gamma(s)\text{ and }\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)=\{b(s)\}\}\).

definitions.name: Fourth-cumulant fiber region
definitions.construction: Clip every empirical raw moment of total degree one through four to \([-\sqrt{V_8},\sqrt{V_8}]\); compute \(\widehat\kappa_{iTTT}\), replace \(\widehat\kappa_{TTTT}\) by its maximum with \((3/2)a_{\min}^4\), set \(\widehat a_T=(\widehat\kappa_{TTTT}/3)^{1/4}\), \(\widehat a_i=\widehat\kappa_{iTTT}/(3\widehat a_T^3)\), form \(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\), and return the declared union \(C_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\) with radius \(L_\beta C_{\mathrm{Lap}}r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\).
inputs: a known literal standardized-Laplace source law

statements.statement: For each \(u\in\mathcal R\), \(-2t^{-2}\log|\phi_X(tu)|\to u^\top\Gamma u\) as \(|t|\to\infty\); coordinate and pair-sum polarization therefore identify every entry of \(\Gamma\) from \(P_X\).
statements.justification: This is the population bridge from the observed law to the causal covariance.
statements.gap: Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi's Theorems 2--3 identify a finite SCM class under mutually independent nonconstant Gaussian-indecomposable sources, \(1\le k\le p\), lexicographically ordered loading columns, and full column rank; they do not state this greatest-divisor ray functional or a sampling region for it.
statements.consumer: It lets an analyst audit covariance identification without estimating latent source labels.

statements.statement: The full compatible effect fiber has the exact representation \(\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)=\{\beta_J(\Gamma):J\in\mathcal J\}\). Moreover, it is a singleton if and only if \(\gamma_{TW\cdot(D\cup J)}(\Gamma)\gamma_{YW\cdot(D\cup J\cup\{T\})}(\Gamma)=0\) for every ideal edge \(J\to J\cup\{W\}\).
statements.justification: The proposition replaces a factorial order list by the exact treatment-predecessor lattice and exposes all effect-collision strata.
statements.gap: Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi bounds the number of equivalent SCMs and Perkovi\'c--Kalisch--Maathuis enumerates possible effects, but neither inspected source gives this ideal-indexed equality or local singleton certificate.
statements.consumer: The representation is the population specification needed by an IDA-style effect report under a known partial order.

statements.statement: For positive-definite \(H,H'\) with spectra in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\), \(d_H(\Theta_{TY}(H,\preceq),\Theta_{TY}(H',\preceq))\le L_\beta\|H-H'\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), including points at which distinct ideal branches coincide.
statements.justification: Hausdorff stability is the margin-free transfer principle from covariance uncertainty to set-valued causal uncertainty.
statements.gap: Structure-uncertainty papers emphasize nonsmoothness of selected effects; the set-valued map admits a uniform bound without a swap margin.
statements.consumer: Any valid covariance region can be converted into a whole-fiber region without testing which effects collide.

statements.statement: The construction in \(\mathrm{def:ray\text{-}region}\) is measurable and satisfies \(\inf_{P_X\in\mathcal M}P_X^N\{\Gamma\in K_N\}\ge1-\alpha_N\) for every \(N\). On the active branch, simultaneously \(|z_u-u^\top\Gamma u|\le w_N\) for all \(u\in\mathcal R\) and \(\|\widehat\Gamma_N-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\Delta_N\).
statements.justification: A finite-sample simultaneous event, not a pointwise asymptotic estimator, is needed for honest propagation through all order branches.
statements.gap: Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov supplies characteristic-function concentration and polarization for covariance estimation; the explicit centered fixed-envelope region and bounded fallback are specialized here for honest causal projection.
statements.consumer: It gives an auditable covariance uncertainty object before causal enumeration begins.

statements.statement: For every \(N\), \(\inf_{P_X\in\mathcal M}P_X^N\{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\subseteq C_N\}\ge1-\alpha\). On the simultaneous covariance event, \(\operatorname{ex}(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq))\le4L_\beta\Delta_N\). This is a finite-sample simultaneous whole-fiber guarantee unavailable from Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1 of Wang--Kolar--Drton: those results start from an asymptotically valid confidence set for a true ordering and asymptotically valid conditional adjustment-set intervals to cover one total effect, whereas \(C_N\) contains every element of the partially identified fiber on one event. The underlying regimes are nonnested: \(\mathcal M\setminus\mathcal W_{\mathrm{WKD}}\ne\varnothing\) because generic common non-Gaussian source loadings on multiple coordinates yield latent dependence that violates their mutually independent additive-error representation and its residual--regressor order certificate, while \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{WKD}}\setminus\mathcal M\ne\varnothing\) because identifiable additive-error laws may have characteristic-function zeros on a named ray or no positive Gaussian divisor and hence violate the maintained Fourier lower envelope or \(\Gamma\succeq\lambda I\).
statements.justification: The theorem supplies finite-sample simultaneous coverage of the complete mixed-noise effect fiber, rather than asymptotic coverage of one effect after order-confidence and adjustment-set steps.
statements.gap: Wang--Kolar--Drton's Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1 work in a causally sufficient recursive additive-error model with mutually independent centered coordinate errors and order identifiability from nonlinear functions or linear non-Gaussian errors; their effect interval is asymptotically valid for one total effect conditional on order-set and adjustment-interval validity. The present nonnested model permits latent common sources, identifies a greatest Gaussian divisor by Fourier tails, and gives finite-sample simultaneous inclusion of every partial-order-compatible Cholesky effect.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{pcalg::ida}\) workflow can report a confidence-enlarged set of all compatible effects rather than a selected list.

statements.statement: If \(c<C\), then uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), \(\mathbb E\|\widehat\Gamma_N-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O((\log N)^{-1})\), \(\mathbb E d_H(\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N,\preceq),\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq))=O((\log N)^{-1})\), and \(\mathbb E d_H(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq))=O((\log N)^{-1})\).
statements.justification: The theorem quantifies both estimation loss and the excess size of an honest set.
statements.gap: The logarithmic covariance rate is known from Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov; uniform expected Hausdorff control for the entire causal fiber is not stated there.
statements.consumer: It supplies a rate for the minimum absolute compatible effect, a one-Lipschitz IDA ranking summary.

statements.statement: Can the handle in \(\mathrm{def:lower\text{-}handle}\) produce Borel laws \(P_{0,N},P_{1,N}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}\) for every sufficiently large \(N\), with \(\Gamma(P_{0,N})=\Gamma(0)\), \(\Gamma(P_{1,N})=\Gamma(s_N)\), \(s_N\asymp(\log N)^{-1}\), and \(\|P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}-P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0\)? The construction must establish global density positivity, full-column-rank membership under the unit-variance source normalization, the common ray envelopes, the fixed eighth moment, greatest-divisor status in every direction, and the uniform weighted-Plancherel derivative bound for the six-degree Laplace--Student splice.
statements.justification: This analytic construction is the genuine open content needed to make the causal logarithmic lower bound valid inside one fixed smooth moment class.
statements.gap: Meister and Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov use Fourier compensation for scalar or covariance lower bounds, but their displayed pairs do not supply this moment-compatible causal collision path.
statements.consumer: A positive answer activates the conditional Le Cam converse for uniformly honest whole-fiber procedures even when every compatible order has the same effect.

statements.statement: Conditional on an affirmative construction in \(\mathrm{oeq:smooth\text{-}splice}\), \(\inf_{\widetilde\Gamma_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Gamma,N}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\asymp(\log N)^{-1}\) and \(\inf_{\widetilde\Theta_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Theta,N}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}d_H(\widetilde\Theta_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq))\asymp(\log N)^{-1}\). Moreover, for every \((S_N)\in\mathfrak C_\alpha(\mathcal M_\star)\), the constructed collision laws satisfy \(\liminf_{N\to\infty}P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}\{\operatorname{diam}(S_N)\ge|b(s_N)-b(0)|\}\ge1-2\alpha\), where \(P_{0,N},P_{1,N}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}\) and \(|b(s_N)-b(0)|\asymp(\log N)^{-1}\).
statements.justification: The conditional implication makes the precise statistical consequences of the unresolved analytic construction auditable without asserting that construction as settled.
statements.gap: Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov proves a covariance minimax theorem; conditional on the displayed fixed-class pair, this statement adds singleton causal-effect loss and a quantified honest-confidence diameter event on an exact collision stratum.
statements.consumer: Once the open construction is verified, it prevents an IDA implementation from advertising uniformly faster mixed-noise effect precision by order selection or collision testing.

statements.statement: The map \(F_{p,M_8,a_{\min}}\) is globally Lipschitz on \([-\sqrt{V_8},\sqrt{V_8}]^{d_4}\), and the quotient modulus \(C_{\mathrm{Lap}}\) is finite. This bound holds across the maximum-floor kink and the spectral-clipping eigenvalue kinks because the maximum is Lipschitz, the fourth-root and reciprocal powers are Lipschitz above the positive floor, the intervening moment maps are polynomials on a compact cube, and spectral projection is nonexpansive in Frobenius norm.
statements.justification: A global modulus is required because derivative suprema do not control the nonsmooth floor and spectral projection at their kinks.
statements.gap: Fourth-moment ICA limit theory is local; this lemma supplies the finite-sample global propagation bound needed by the bounded construction.
statements.consumer: It validates a single finite-sample radius for every law in the literal-Laplace class.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}\), the fourth-cumulant construction satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(N^{-1/2})\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}d_H(\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}},\preceq),\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq))=O(N^{-1/2})\), and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}P^{\otimes N}\{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\subseteq C_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(N\).
statements.justification: The theorem locates a transparent parametric boundary of the severely ill-posed Fourier class.
statements.gap: Miettinen--Taskinen--Nordhausen--Oja derives fourth-moment ICA limits, but not finite-sample whole-fiber coverage for a greatest Gaussian divisor.
statements.consumer: Audited literal-Laplace applications can use root-\(N\) uncertainty rather than the conservative logarithmic region.

sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from one fixed mixed-noise law \(P_X\).
sampling_model.treatment: The coordinate \(T\) is intervened upon in each compatible linear structural model; no treatment assignment is randomized in the observed sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; stability is supplied by \(\lambda I\preceq\Gamma\preceq\Lambda I\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Source scales are normalized to unit variance before imposing \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le A_{\max}\), with full-column-rank, sign, and lexicographic loading conventions. The explicitly maintained greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance is recovered from centered empirical characteristic-function moduli on coordinate and pair-sum rays; the uniformly quantified literal-Laplace subclass instead uses clipped fourth cumulants and a global Lipschitz modulus.

estimand_functional: \(\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)=\{\gamma_{YT\cdot(D\cup J)}(\Gamma)/\gamma_{TT\cdot(D\cup J)}(\Gamma):J\in\mathcal J\}\), estimated by the simultaneous interval union \(C_N\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 2--4 and \(1\le k\le p\), Theorems 2--3 give at most \(p!\) equivalent mixed-noise SCMs and uniqueness once the causal order is known.
Theorems 5--6 give matching logarithmic minimax rates for latent Gaussian covariance estimation under nonparametric contamination.
The paper gives scalar centered Fourier variance estimation and least-favorable unknown-Gaussian-variance pairs under fixed smoothness envelopes.
The paper constructs test-inversion confidence regions for total effects under structure uncertainty and equal error variances.
The paper gives generic total-effect identification and rigorous confidence regions under structure uncertainty using partial equality restrictions on structural-error variances.
Algorithm 3 unions adjustment-set intervals over retained orders; Lemma 1 gives asymptotic coverage of one effect from order-set and conditional-interval validity.
The paper adapts IDA and joint IDA to maximal PDAGs with background knowledge.
The paper derives estimating equations and asymptotic distributions for fourth-moment ICA procedures.
The paper constructs multiplier-bootstrap uniform deconvolution bands with an unknown error law and an auxiliary error sample.

tldr: Under mutually independent, unit-variance, nonconstant Gaussian-indecomposable latent sources, a full-column-rank identified loading convention, and an explicitly maintained greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition, a known partial order leaves a finite Cholesky-effect fiber. The project represents that fiber by treatment-predecessor ideals and maps one measurable finite-sample characteristic-function covariance region into simultaneous coverage of every compatible effect without separation at collisions. This guarantee is theorem-level distinct from Wang--Kolar--Drton's Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1: their causally sufficient identifiable additive-error model yields asymptotic coverage of one effect after order and adjustment-set inference, whereas the present latent mixed-noise regime is nonnested and receives finite-sample whole-fiber coverage. Expected Hausdorff error is logarithmic on fixed ordinary-smooth envelopes; a matching collision-stratum converse remains conditional on the open smooth-splice construction. Literal standardized-Laplace sources form a root-\(N\) fourth-cumulant boundary.

project_justification.gap: Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi give finite population identification for mixed-noise models, while Wang--Kolar--Drton's Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1 propagate an asymptotic confidence set for an identifiable additive-error ordering into coverage of one total effect. Neither gives a finite-sample event covering every partial-order-compatible effect after greatest-Gaussian-divisor recovery under latent common sources; the two law classes are nonnested, and the moment-compatible collision lower pair remains open.
project_justification.niche: Fixed-dimensional latent mixed-noise systems with normalized sources, audited ordinary-smooth ray envelopes, an explicit greatest-divisor condition, and genuine partial-order ambiguity require inference for a set-valued effect target rather than selection of an identifiable additive-error order.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the predecessor-ideal functional, an explicit centered ray region with clipping and fallback, a theorem-level nonnesting comparison and finite-sample simultaneous whole-fiber guarantee, a conditional route to the fixed-class logarithmic converse, and a literal-Laplace boundary controlled by a global Lipschitz modulus.

related_work: Sanjaroonpouri and Ramazi are the population anchor: their Assumptions 2--4 and Theorems 2--3 use mutually independent nonconstant sources with no Gaussian convolution factor, \(1\le k\le p\), lexicographically ordered loading columns, and full column rank to obtain a finite Cholesky-indexed SCM class. The greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition here is an additional maintained model condition, not an inherited consequence of that theorem or of the finite-ray envelopes. Wang, Kolar, and Drton study recursive additive-error SEMs \(Z_v=f_v(Z_{\operatorname{pa}(v)})+\epsilon_v\) with mutually independent centered coordinate errors and target settings in which nonlinear functions or linear non-Gaussian errors identify causal order. Their Algorithm 3 unions adjustment-set intervals over orderings retained at level \(1-\alpha/2\), and Lemma 1 derives asymptotic coverage of one total effect from pointwise order-set inclusion and conditional interval validity. It neither supplies finite-sample simultaneous coverage of every member of a partially identified fiber nor recovers a greatest Gaussian divisor. The comparison is nonnested: latent common-source laws in \(\mathcal M\) generically violate their independent-error representation, while their identifiable additive-error class allows laws with ray zeros or without a positive Gaussian divisor, which violate \(\mathcal M\). Belomestny, Trabs, and Tsybakov are the multivariate donor for characteristic-function polarization and logarithmic covariance recovery. Meister is the scalar donor for fixed-envelope centering and Fourier-compensated lower pairs. Strieder and Drton's equal-variance work treats effect size and causal-structure uncertainty jointly. Their 2024 partial-homoscedasticity paper uses equality restrictions among structural-error variances in causally sufficient linear models; it neither identifies a Gaussian convolution divisor under latent non-Gaussian sources nor simultaneously covers the present partial-order Cholesky fiber on collision strata. Perkovi\'c, Kalisch, and Maathuis connect background knowledge to IDA effect multisets. Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja provide fourth-cumulant estimating equations and pointwise limit theory. Kato and Sasaki give honest Fourier-domain bands with an auxiliary error sample.
technical_internal_limitation: The matching lower claim is conditional on completing the uniform Fourier-derivative and weighted-Plancherel estimates for the six-degree smooth Laplace--Student splice. Positivity, full-column-rank membership after unit-variance normalization, the common envelopes, the fixed eighth moment, greatest-divisor status in every direction, and product-experiment indistinguishability must all hold with constants fixed before \(N\) varies. Failure of any one condition removes the matching lower and honest-diameter consequences but leaves the exact fiber and upper confidence construction intact.
honest_scope: The exact ideal representation, Lipschitz transfer, finite-sample region, logarithmic upper rate, theorem-level separation from the Wang--Kolar--Drton order-to-effect construction, and uniformly quantified literal-Laplace boundary are theorem targets. The predecessor-ideal representation is a supporting result rather than the field-tier novelty center. The smooth-splice pair and therefore the matching minimax and honest-diameter conclusions are explicitly open; the lower theorem is only the conditional Le Cam implication. The greatest-divisor characterization is an explicit model condition distinct from Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi's primitive source assumptions. Dimension, spectral bounds, loading bound after unit-variance normalization, ray exponents, and envelope constants are fixed and known. The proposal does not claim adaptive unknown-exponent inference, growing-dimension guarantees, polynomial-delay ideal enumeration, correct singleton selection, or minimax sharpness for every exponent profile. Sanity corollary: when \(\preceq\) is a total order, \(\mathcal J\) has one treatment-predecessor ideal and the fiber is the standard singleton regression effect \(\gamma_{YT\cdot D}(\Gamma)/\gamma_{TT\cdot D}(\Gamma)\); with known \(\Gamma\), there is no statistical inflation.

seed_details.opportunity: Replace population finite identification by a measurable finite-sample region that covers every partial-order-compatible Cholesky effect at once.

literature_map: Sanjaroonpouri and Ramazi, Assumptions 2--4, Theorems 2--3, and Corollary 2, use mutually independent nonconstant sources without Gaussian convolution factors, \(1\le k\le p\), lexicographically ordered loading columns, and full column rank to identify a finite Cholesky-indexed equivalence class, but do not state the present greatest-divisor sampling region. Wang, Kolar, and Drton specify recursive additive-error equations with mutually independent centered coordinate errors and motivate order identifiability through nonlinear functions or linear non-Gaussian errors. Their Algorithm 3 forms a union of conditional regression intervals over retained adjustment sets, and Lemma 1 gives asymptotic coverage of one total effect assuming pointwise inclusion of a valid ordering and validity of its conditional interval. Their class and \(\mathcal M\) are nonnested: generic latent common-source laws violate mutually independent coordinate errors, while identifiable additive-error laws may violate the positive ray envelope or lack a positive Gaussian divisor. Belomestny, Trabs, and Tsybakov, equations (4)--(5) and Theorems 1, 5, and 6, use characteristic-function log moduli, coordinate and pair-sum polarization, and Fourier testing for logarithmic latent-covariance recovery. Meister, equations (2), (4), and (16)--(18), supplies scalar fixed-envelope centering and least-favorable variance compensation. Strieder and Drton's 2023 paper constructs effect regions under equal-variance structure uncertainty; their 2024 paper uses partial structural-error variance equalities in causally sufficient linear models, not mixed-noise divisor recovery. Perkovi\'c, Kalisch, and Maathuis adapt IDA to background knowledge. Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja derive fourth-moment ICA limits. Kato and Sasaki construct deconvolution bands with an auxiliary error sample. No inspected result combines greatest-divisor recovery, finite-sample simultaneous coverage of the complete partial-order effect fiber at collisions, and the stated cumulant boundary.

novelty_justification: The closest population result is Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi's finite mixed-noise SCM identification, and the closest statistical donor is Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov's latent Gaussian covariance recovery. The direct causal-inference comparator is Wang--Kolar--Drton: Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1 turn an asymptotically valid confidence set for an identifiable additive-error ordering plus conditional adjustment-set intervals into asymptotic coverage of one total effect. Theorem 2 establishes the strict regime-and-guarantee distinction: the published additive-error class and the present latent mixed-noise class are nonnested, and the explicit characteristic-function event gives finite-sample simultaneous inclusion of every point of the partial-order Cholesky fiber, including coincident branches, without order selection. Strieder--Drton's partial-homoscedasticity regions are also adjacent but rely on structural-error variance equalities in a causally sufficient model. Proposition 2 is supporting algebra rather than the novelty center. The field-tier case rests on the mixed-noise whole-fiber theorem together with the conditional matched logarithmic frontier; the smooth-splice construction remains openly unresolved. Scalar centering, polarization, and fourth-cumulant recovery are donors rather than novelty.
